papers.title_in_file: Single photon imaging and sensing of obscured objects around the corner
papers.what_it_is: A proof-of-principle experiment using nonlinear-optical (up-conversion) gated single photon detection for coaxial non-line-of-sight imaging, positioning and vibration sensing of obscured objects.

assertions.value: The authors introduce a non-line-of-sight imaging and sensing approach that uses picosecond gated single photon detection generated by quantum frequency conversion.
quotes: Here, we introduce a new approach to NLOS imaging and sensing using the picosecond gated single photon detection generated by quantum frequency conversion.

assertions.value: The authors report that 4×10−3 detected photons per pulse per pixel are needed to position and profile occluded objects with high resolution.
quotes: For each pixel, only 4×10−3 photons are needed to be detected per pulse to position and proﬁle occluded objects with high resolution.

assertions.value: The authors report that reconstructing the obscured arrowhead image required only about 4 × 10−3 detected information-carrying NLOS photon counts per pulse per pixel at the peak of the time-resolved histograms, which they attribute to the very low noise of the NGSPD.
assertions.anchor: NLOS imaging of highly obscured target, p.9
quotes: only about 4 × 10−3 detected information-carrying NLOS photon counts per pulse
per pixel is required at the peak of the time-resolved histograms, thanks to the very low noise
assertions.reader_inference: The figure is a peak value per pixel, not a mean over the scene.

assertions.value: The authors state that vibration frequencies of different objects can be resolved by analyzing the photon number fluctuation received within a ten-picosecond window, allowing NLOS acoustic sensing.
quotes: the vibration frequencies of different objects can be resolved by analyzing the photon number ﬂuctuation received within in a ten-picosecond window, allowing NLOS acoustic sensing.

assertions.value: The authors describe the setup as a mode-locked laser, a MEMS scanning mirror, a single-mode fiber coaxial optical transceiver, a programmable optical delay line and a silicon SPAD.
quotes: The setup consists of a mode-locked laser (MLL), a micro-electromechanical-system (MEMS) scanning mirror, a single-mode ﬁber (SMF) coaxial optical transceiver, a programmable optical delay line (ODL) and a silicon SPAD.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors state the hidden scene uses a 2-inch diameter metallic diffuser as the wall and an aluminum mesh (1 mm diameter wire grid with 2 x 2 mm openings) as the obscurant before the hidden object.
quotes: The scene around the corner is realized by using a 2-inch diameter metallic diffuser as the wall, an aluminum mesh (1 mm diameter wire grid with 2 x 2 mm openings) as the obscurant before the hidden object.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors state a time-correlated 6-ps pump pulse acts as a narrow nonlinear optical gate that up-converts a 6-ps signal photon by sum-frequency generation, and that the resulting window is much narrower than the detector and electronics timing jitter.
quotes: where a time correlated 6-ps
pump pulse performs effectively as a narrow nonlinear optical gating to up-convert 6-ps signal photon via sum-frequency generation
a high extinction picosecond photon detection window much narrower than timing jitter of the detector and its associated electronics
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer joins page 4 and 5 text; the two 6-ps values are later given as 6.6 ps and 6.1 ps (Methods).

assertions.value: The authors state that signal photons are effectively up-converted only if they are temporally aligned with the pump pulse, lie in the phase-matched wavelength for the pump, and are in the fundamental temporal-frequency mode of the pump.
quotes: can be effectively upconverted into sum-frequency photons only if they are 1) temporally aligned with the pump pulse; 2) lying in the phase matched wavelength for the pump; and 3) in the fundamental TF mode of the pump.
assertions.certainty_reason: The Methods state the detector's operating condition.

assertions.value: The authors state that prior NLOS reconstruction methods, with few exceptions, require a priori information on the hidden scene and are restricted to hidden objects of known geometry.
quotes: require a priori information on the hidden scene and are hence overly restricted to imaging the hidden and obscured objects of known geometry.

assertions.value: The authors state a major drawback is the need to delay the gating pump pulse to retrieve arrival time, which makes acquisition time-consuming and limits the imaging depth.
quotes: One major drawback of the current NGSPD approach is the need of temporally delay the gating pump pulse
which makes the data acquisition time-consuming and limits the imaging depth.
assertions.certainty_reason: The Discussion states this limit of its own system.

assertions.value: The authors propose multi-wavelength phase matching to up-convert two or more wavelength bands in one waveguide, and a higher repetition rate pump with a correlated time tagger, to cut acquisition time and extend depth; these are not demonstrated.
quotes: multi wavelength phase matching enables up-converting two or even more wavelength bands in one waveguide
which will reduce the acquisition time by times of the multi peak numbers.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that the system can perform NLOS imaging and sensing in complex environments, including obscured and partially occluded objects, without complex reconstruction models, and name machine-learning single-illumination-point reconstruction as future work.
quotes: can perform NLOS imaging and sensing over realistic, complex environment, including those of obscured and partially occluded objects, yet without complex reconstruction models.
reconstructing NLOS spatial information with only single illumination point aided by machine learning
assertions.reader_inference: Demonstrations use one wire-mesh obscurant, retroreflective targets and a 2-inch diffuser; broader realism is not tested.
